The feature works both via CLI and via the config file. Summary of changes:

- `src/assets/ignored_suffixes.rs`: added a `custom_suffixes` vector (default empty), a `custom_suffixes()` accessor, and `add_custom_suffix()`
- `src/syntax_mapping.rs`: added `SyntaxMapping::add_ignored_suffix()` (src/syntax_mapping.rs:159)
- `src/assets.rs`: custom suffixes are now included in the suffix-stripping chain during syntax detection (src/assets.rs:332)
- `src/bin/bat/clap_app.rs`: added the `--ignored-suffix <suffix>` option (repeatable, so multiple suffixes can be listed)
- `src/bin/bat/app.rs`: values from the CLI (or `~/.config/bat/config`, since config-file args are merged into argv before parsing) are passed into the syntax mapping (src/bin/bat/app.rs:123)

Validation:
- `ignored_suffix_arg` test passes; lib tests (37) and bin tests (6) pass; all 79 integration tests pass (the one excluded, `no_args_doesnt_break`, aborts with an "IO Safety violation" SIGABRT that occurs identically on the pristine baseline — an environment issue, not caused by this change)
- Manual check confirmed `.json.example` gets JSON highlighting with `--ignored-suffix=".example"` in the bat config file, and plain output without it
